quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is discouraged.
Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen by them.
Be close to the road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen by them.
questions.explanation: The right lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It also keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: To get the best protection, wear a helmet that:

options.text: Fits snugly.
Is well-worn and broken in.
Is pretty loose.
Does not have a chinstrap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no defects.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Restricts your side vision.
Can greatly reduce the severity of head injuries.
Is usually uncomfortable.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce the severity of head injuries.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injuries in a crash. It will not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not cover your arms or legs completely.
Should not include a jacket if the weather is warm.
Can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly but allow you to move freely.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants:

options.text: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
Should be loose and flap in the wind while you ride.
Should only partially cover your arms and legs.
Should be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but allow free movement. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact force. This prevents the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Is a useless action.
Lets you use engine braking.
Is illegal.
Should not be done if other vehicles are around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Engine braking by smoothly downshifting is a useful option. Use your brake lights separately to tell other drivers you are slowing down.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Wear long pants.
Wear shorts if it is warm outside.
Wear loose-fitting clothing.
Wear sandals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear long pants.
questions.explanation: Wear durable pants and a jacket that cover your arms and legs completely. Any exposed skin is at risk in a crash.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it difficult to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Help other drivers identify you.
Improve your grip on the handlebars.
Offer no protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Improve your grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: A cushion of space while riding helps you to:

options.text: Have time to react to hazards.
Hide from other drivers.
Prevent yourself from avoiding hazards.
Look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A cushion of space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothes should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but not your legs.
Cover your legs completely, but not your arms.
Be whatever is comfortable, even if not safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: To stay protected while riding, wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume they have ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
Not let them ask questions.
Not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to ride safely. Never assume they know what to do. Give them full instructions before every ride.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A dirt or gravel road
A strip of oil in the center of a lane
Mud on pavement
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal covers are all slippery and dangerous. Dry pavement is not slippery.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to grip the handgrips better.
Not be worn because they make controls harder to use.
Be worn only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to grip the handgrips better.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handgrips and protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: The best thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened tightly.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened tightly.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened tightly is the single most important thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should be done:

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Twice a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This takes only a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you ride.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects are:

options.text: Much stronger than when either is used alone.
Less dangerous than when either is used alone.
Usually not serious.
Usually balanced out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Much stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can impair your riding. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should wear:

options.text: Dark-colored clothes.
Bright-colored clothes.
Lights.
A black jacket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors so other drivers can see you. Choose clothes that make you visible day and night.

questions.question: When preparing to pass, ride in the left part of your lane because:

options.text: It helps you see ahead better.
It makes it harder to see ahead.
It makes it hard to see past the vehicle.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see ahead better.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see ahead and makes other drivers more likely to see you.
